body_zh: 在发生一系列道德案件后，国会的性骚扰规则正在接受审查 - ABC News
在发生一系列道德案件后，国会的性骚扰规则正在接受审查
在国会山审查性骚扰问题的立法者表示，他们对所发现的情况感到不安
华盛顿——当众议员凯特·卡马克今年春天开始组建一个打击国会山不当性行为的特别工作组时，这位佛罗里达州共和党人很快就收到了前工作人员的来信，他们希望分享自己的故事。
她说，他们“从木制品中脱颖而出”，并保持沉默，因为众所周知，站出来将是他们辛辛苦苦取得的职业生涯的终结。
“这些是最难进行的对话，”卡马克说。 “这些故事令人心痛。”
今年众议院道德委员会有关不当性行为的调查激增，促使国会领导人成立了一个由卡马克和新墨西哥州众议员特蕾莎·莱杰·费尔南德斯领导的工作组。卡马克说，他们的发现令人不安。
受害者不清楚可以去哪里寻求帮助。他们不相信肇事者会受到惩罚。目前举报骚扰的要求可能对他们不利，例如在涉嫌违规后提出索赔有 180 天的“限制”。
“这是一场灾难，”卡马克说。 “国会山的整个系统实际上是为了给受害者制造寒蝉效应。”
该工作组预计将在 11 月 3 日选举后发布修改建议，目标是在年底前采取行动。
今年国会除了维持联邦政府的运转之外，还一直在努力做更多的事情，而众议院道德委员会却卷入了华盛顿发生的一些重大事件的中间。
今年，三名议员辞职，以免面临驱逐投票的前景。其中两起案件涉及涉嫌不当性行为。另一名成员因与两名女助手的互动而受到谴责。其他调查正在进行中。
这些故事出现之际，国会正面临公众对政府处理杰弗里·爱泼斯坦案的愤怒。在过去的几个月里，民主妇女核心小组的成员与幸存者举行了多次会议，她们推动司法部公布与爱泼斯坦相关的文件。
四月，道德委员会开始调查当时的众议员是否。加利福尼亚州民主党人埃里克·斯瓦尔韦尔 (Eric Swalwell) 对在他监督下工作的一名员工实施了不当性行为。斯瓦尔韦尔很快就辞职了，因为同事们呼吁将他开除。
同样，德克萨斯州共和党众议员托尼·冈萨雷斯(Tony Gonzales)辞职，因为委员会正在调查他是否对办公室的一名员工有不当性行为。冈萨雷斯承认与一名工作人员有染，该工作人员后来自杀身亡。
最近，委员会建议对北卡罗来纳州共和党众议员查克·爱德华兹（Chuck Edwards）进行谴责，调查得出结论，他对办公室的两名年轻女职员持续存在不专业和不当的行为。众议院以 413 票对 2 票通过了这项建议。
加利福尼亚州民主党众议员吉米·戈麦斯也是委员会调查的对象，因为他可能与众议院工作人员发生了不当性行为。戈麦斯表示，他将配合调查，但也强调，他的行为本质上是双方同意的，没有违反法律或众议院道德规则。他还向家人和选民道歉。
该委员会还在调查佛罗里达州共和党众议员科里·米尔斯是否存在不当性行为或约会暴力等指控。米尔斯否认了这些指控，并在最近的共和党初选中落败。
卡马克说，随着委员会审理的一些案件的故事开始浮出水面，她和同事们开始讨论他们可以采取哪些措施来“清理众议院”。她向路易斯安那州共和党众议员迈克·约翰逊寻求加入的机会。

title_en: This US House district was once a political battleground. Now it shows why Congress is dysfunctional
title_zh: 这个美国众议院选区曾经是一个政治战场。现在它显示了为什么国会功能失调
summary: The number of politically competitive U.S. House seats is shrinking rapidly
summary_zh: 美国众议院政治竞争席位数量正在迅速减少
body_en: This US House district was once a political battleground. Now it shows why Congress is dysfunctional
The number of politically competitive U.S. House seats is shrinking rapidly

RALEIGH, N.C. -- In 2022, Democrat Wiley Nickel ran as a moderate and narrowly won North Carolina's 13th Congressional District by about 9,000 votes. Two years later, the current congressman, Republican Brad Knott, ran as a conservative and coasted into the U.S. House by more than 70,000 votes.
Voters didn't change their minds. Politicians changed their voters.

The Republican-controlled legislature redrew the state's congressional map to transform what was one of the last remaining swing districts in the South to a safe GOP seat. Lawmakers split the rectangular 13th District into an hourglass shape that carved out Democratic voters in Raleigh and replaced them with a swath of rural counties reaching up to the Virginia border.

Swing seats, meaning a district that a presidential candidate won by 5 percentage points or fewer in the previous election, are disappearing from the national map. For decades after World War II, the number of competitive seats in the House slowly eroded as the United States grew more polarized , voters were less likely to split their ticket between parties and people moved closer to like-minded neighbors, creating Democratic strongholds in urban areas and Republicans ones across rural America.

That decline accelerated over the past year after Republican President Donald Trump sparked a partisan redistricting battle. The number of swing districts fell from 45 to 37. There were 96 House seats that fit the modern definition of a swing seat in 1964, according to one count from the 1970s, when the shrinking number of such districts was first noted.
That means the overwhelming majority of House seats are effectively won in primaries , with the support of only a fraction of voters who usually are at the extreme ideological end of their party.
Nickel saw the impact firsthand during his lone term in Washington.

“The biggest divide I found in Congress wasn’t Democrat versus Republican, it was safe seats versus competitive seats,” Nickel said. “When your focus is on running a campaign where you talk to every single voter, you look at things differently and your focus is on solving problems.”
Unite America, an organization pushing alternatives to party primaries, calculated that 87% of the representatives elected to the House in 2024 were chosen by 7% of the country’s voters.

“Voters don’t have any way of holding Congress responsible, except for a narrow window of swing districts,” Nick Troiano, the group's executive director, said in an interview, adding that he expects things to get worse in November. “The least competitive election of our lifetimes will lead to the least accountable and least representative Congress of our lifetimes.”
Republicans are hoping the smaller number of competitive seats puts a low ceiling on what Democrats can win on Nov. 3.
“Both sides are fighting over a narrow House battlefield,” said Mike Marinella, a spokesman for the National Republican Congressional Campaign. “It's a knife fight in a dark alley.”
The alley may be widening this year , but it still is an alley.

Democrats have expanded their political targets, given the unpopular war with Iran and voters angry about high prices. Both parties are spending on campaigns in Republican area that normally would not be competitive.
Even in what is shaping up as a difficult political environment, however, Republicans are protected by the limited number of seats in play.
“Even if there's the kind of swing we got in 2006, there's not going to be 40 seats changing hands. There's going to be 20 seats changing hands,” said Ian Shapiro, a Yale political scientist.

There is a long-standing debate among academics as to how much of the decline can be blamed on partisan-motivated redistricting , known as gerrymandering, and how much on Americans' increasing proclivity to live among like-minded people who vote the same way. Multiple studies have found that without partisan gerrymandering, the House would have about double the number of competitive seats it has now.
One thing most agree on is that the diminishment of competitive seats leads to greater polarization because legislators are only beholden to primary voters.
body_zh: 这个美国众议院选区曾经是一个政治战场。现在它显示了国会功能失调的原因 - ABC News
这个美国众议院选区曾经是一个政治战场。现在它显示了为什么国会功能失调
美国众议院政治竞争席位数量正在迅速减少
北卡罗来纳州罗利——2022 年，民主党人威利·尼克尔 (Wiley Nickel) 作为温和派参选，以约 9,000 票微弱优势赢得北卡罗来纳州第 13 国会选区。两年后，现任国会议员、共和党人布拉德·诺特以保守派身份参选，并以超过 7 万票的优势进入美国众议院。
选民没有改变主意。政客们改变了他们的选民。
共和党控制的立法机构重新绘制了该州的国会地图，将南部仅存的摇摆选区之一转变为共和党的安全席位。立法者将长方形的第 13 选区分割成沙漏形状，将罗利的民主党选民划出，并用延伸至弗吉尼亚州边境的一大片乡村县取而代之。
摇摆席位，即总统候选人在上次选举中以 5 个百分点或更少的优势赢得的选区，正在从国家地图上消失。第二次世界大战后的几十年里，随着美国两极分化加剧，众议院的竞争性席位数量慢慢减少，选民们不太可能在党派之间分配选票，人们也更加接近志同道合的邻居，从而在城市地区建立了民主党的据点，在美国农村地区建立了共和党的据点。
在共和党总统唐纳德·特朗普引发党派重新划分选区之战后，这种下降在过去一年加速。摇摆选区的数量从 45 个减少到 37 个。根据 1970 年代的一项统计，1964 年，众议院有 96 个席位符合摇摆席位的现代定义，当时此类选区的数量首次出现减少。
这意味着绝大多数众议院席位实际上是在初选中赢得的，而只有一小部分选民的支持，而这些选民通常处于党派的极端意识形态一端。
尼克尔在华盛顿的唯一任期内亲眼目睹了这一影响。
“我在国会发现的最大分歧不是民主党与共和党，而是安全席位与竞争性席位，”尼克尔说。 “当你的重点是开展一场与每一位选民交谈的竞选活动时，你会以不同的方式看待事物，你的重点是解决问题。”
推动政党初选替代方案的组织Unite America计算出，2024年当选的众议院代表中有87%是由该国7%的选民选出的。
该组织执行董事尼克·特罗伊亚诺(Nick Troiano)在接受采访时表示，“除了摇摆选区的狭窄窗口之外，选民没有任何办法让国会承担责任。”他补充说，他预计11月情况会变得更糟。 “我们一生中竞争最激烈的选举将导致我们一生中最不负责任和最具代表性的国会。”
共和党人希望竞争性席位数量较少，从而降低民主党在 11 月 3 日获胜的上限。
“双方都在狭小的众议院战场上展开战斗，”全国共和党国会竞选活动发言人迈克·马里内拉 (Mike Marinella) 说。 “这是在黑暗的小巷里进行的一场刀战。”
今年胡同可能会拓宽，但它仍然是胡同。
鉴于与伊朗的战争不受欢迎以及选民对高物价感到愤怒，民主党扩大了他们的政治目标。两党都在共和党地区的竞选活动上投入资金，而这些竞选活动通常不会具有竞争力。
然而，即使在当前艰难的政治环境中，共和党人仍受到有限席位的保护。
“即使出现 2006 年那样的摇摆，也不会有 40 个席位易手。将会有 20 个席位易手，”耶鲁大学政治学家伊恩·夏皮罗 (Ian Shapiro) 表示。
学术界长期以来一直存在争论，即选民人数下降在多大程度上可以归咎于党派动机的选区重新划分，即所谓的不公正划分选区，以及美国人越来越倾向于生活在志同道合、投票方式相同的人中间。多项研究发现，如果没有党派不公正的选区划分，众议院的竞争性席位数量将是现在的两倍左右。

title_en: The 2028 crop hits New Mexico for inaugural ‘Matanza’ rally
title_zh: 2028 年作物登陆新墨西哥州，举办首届“Matanza”集会
summary: The “Fourth in the Nation Matanza Rally” is testing the appetite for a more Latino-specific cultural touchstone to round out the presidential candidate event rotation.
summary_zh: “全国第四届马坦萨集会”正在测试对更具拉丁裔特色的文化试金石的兴趣，以完善总统候选人
body_en: Prospective presidential candidates are known to chew over pork chops on a stick at Iowa’s iconic State Fair. They gather in South Carolina at Rep. Jim Clyburn’s “World Famous Fish Fry.” And they’re all over New Hampshire … well, any chance they get.
New Mexico today is entering the convening conversation with chicharrón at the “Matanza.”

In the long tradition of major state gatherings that have become dead giveaways of politicians’ presidential ambitions, New Mexico is formally stepping into the political fray, with an inaugural “Fourth in the Nation Matanza Rally” hosted by Democratic Sen. Ben Ray Luján designed to introduce the 2028 crop to the state.
What exactly is a Matanza? It’s a “New Mexico election season staple,” Deb Haaland, who was Interior secretary in the Biden administration and is running for New Mexico governor, told POLITICO.
“You dig a big hole in the ground, you build a fire, you put a pig in the coals, and it cooks overnight, and then you share this grand feast along with tortillas and chicharrón,” Haaland said.

Over 1,500 people, local and state leaders and New Mexico’s congressional delegation are gathering to eat and listen to mariachi and local bands at Albuquerque’s International Balloon Museum this afternoon, in part to rally voters to turn out on Nov. 3. Yet the presidential undertones are quite intentional in the new Democratic early nominating state.

“Matanzas typically in New Mexico have centered around family gatherings, weddings, big celebrations, community celebrations, bringing people together,” Luján told POLITICO. It’ll be a “first taste of New Mexico” for 2028ers to introduce themselves to the state.

New Mexico’s entry into the early nominating lineup has set a course for a primary season where some of the Democratic Party’s most elusive voters will be front and center. Some 2028ers will be hearing from voters directly today — among them Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.). Van Hollen has admitted he’s testing the waters for a presidential bid and told POLITICO “this is going to be part of that process.”
Also in the mix is Sen. Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.) — who wanted to be “neighborly” and show up for Luján — and said he’s “considering” a run but won’t make a decision until after the midterms.
“New Mexico is a lot like Arizona. We've got some shared issues and priorities,” Kelly told POLITICO. “And I think, you know, the Southwest is growing in importance, more people are moving here.”

But Luján is offering free advice for visiting Democrats: “Understand that you need to get out and earn the trust back from so many families where we lost support: labor families, union families, Hispanic families.”
Latino voters make up the majority of voters statewide, and together with Nevada they’re poised to dominate the early primary calendar.

“I think that both the fact that Trump betrayed voters when it came to the economy, plus the fact that they did a bait and switch when it came to their immigration policies, has turned off a lot of Hispanic voters,” Van Hollen told POLITICO. “But where Trump was right was recognizing people's economic pain.”
Blue collar work and agriculture run deep in the fabric of the state. “The [border] lines moved on a lot of families,” as Lujan put it — making the “New Mexican” identity particularly potent.

“We're the fifth-largest state in the country,” Haaland told POLITICO. “We have three national labs. We've got veteran services here. … We're also a border state, and so much commerce here in New Mexico happens on our border.”

And Haaland is also adamant about keeping Native Americans at the forefront of the 2028 conversation. “I want any presidential candidates to really know and understand why they need to think about tribes. Why they need to have a plan for Indian tribes when they're working on their platforms,” she said.

If Haaland wins the governorship, she and Luján will be critical touchpoints for 2028ers. Luján, a former DCCC chair, said he’s already started reaching out to potential candidates. And Haaland, through her gubernatorial campaign, has shared the stage with several of them already.

Pete Buttigieg hit the Land of Enchantment last month, campaigning for Haaland and Vasquez in the heavily Latino town of Las Cruces. Sen. Cory Booker (D-N.J.) held a fundraiser in the state in August. Michigan’s Gretchen Whitmer and Illinois’ JB Pritzker have both swung through the state. And Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham has been fielding calls from prospectives , including Rahm Emanuel and Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, who’s supporting Haaland as chair of the Democratic Governors Association.

But today marks the first official 2028 cattle call for the state. Complete with tribal leaders, local business owners and VIP donors, the first Matanza event will test the appetite for a more Latino-specific cultural touchstone that could round out the obligatory presidential candidate event rotation.
“What I hope that being fourth in the nation can create in New Mexico is a better understanding of what's needed across the West, across the Rocky Mountains, the high desert,” Luján told POLITICO.
body_zh: 众所周知，未来的总统候选人会在爱荷华州标志性的州博览会上咀嚼串在棍子上的猪排。他们聚集在南卡罗来纳州众议员吉姆·克莱伯恩的“世界著名炸鱼店”。他们遍布新罕布什尔州……好吧，他们一有机会就来。
新墨西哥州今天将在“马坦萨”与 chicharrón 进行会议。
重大州集会已成为政客总统野心的显露的长期传统，新墨西哥州正式介入政治争端，由民主党参议员本·雷·卢扬 (Ben Ray Luján) 主持的首届“全国第四届马坦萨集会”旨在向该州介绍 2028 年作物。
马坦萨到底是什么？曾担任拜登政府内政部长、正在竞选新墨西哥州州长的德布·哈兰 (Deb Haaland) 告诉《政治》杂志，这是“新墨西哥州选举季的主要内容”。
哈兰德说：“你在地上挖一个大洞，生火，把一头猪放进煤里，煮一夜，然后你就可以和玉米饼和辣椒一起分享这顿盛宴。”
今天下午，超过 1,500 人、地方和州领导人以及新墨西哥州国会代表团齐聚阿尔伯克基国际气球博物馆，一边吃饭一边听墨西哥流浪乐队和当地乐队的表演，部分原因是为了召集选民在 11 月 3 日投票。然而，在这个新的民主党提前提名州，总统的语气是有意为之的。
卢扬告诉《政治》杂志：“新墨西哥州的马坦萨斯活动通常以家庭聚会、婚礼、大型庆祝活动、社区庆祝活动以及将人们聚集在一起为中心。”对于 2028 年的人们来说，这将是“第一次品尝新墨西哥州”，向该州介绍自己。
新墨西哥州进入早期提名阵容已经为初选赛季奠定了基础，民主党中一些最难以捉摸的选民将成为焦点。一些 2028 支持者今天将直接听取选民的意见，其中包括参议员克里斯·范·霍伦（马里兰州民主党人）。范霍伦承认他正在试水总统竞选，并告诉《政治》杂志“这将是这一过程的一部分。”
参议员马克·凯利（亚利桑那州民主党人）也参与其中，他希望表现得“睦邻友好”并出席卢汉竞选，并表示他正在“考虑”参选，但要到中期选举后才会做出决定。
“新墨西哥州很像亚利桑那州。我们有一些共同的问题和优先事项，”凯利告诉《政治》杂志。 “我认为，你知道，西南部的重要性越来越大，越来越多的人搬到这里。”
但卢扬为来访的民主党人提供免费建议：“要明白，你需要走出去，赢得许多我们失去支持的家庭的信任：劳工家庭、工会家庭、西班牙裔家庭。”
拉丁裔选民占全州选民的大多数，他们与内华达州一起准备在早期初选日程中占据主导地位。
范霍伦告诉《政治》杂志：“我认为，特朗普在经济问题上背叛了选民，加上他们在移民政策上做了诱饵和改变，这已经让很多西班牙裔选民失去了兴趣。” “但特朗普的正确之处在于认识到人们的经济痛苦。”
蓝领工作和农业在该州根深蒂固。正如卢扬所说，“[边境]线对很多家庭产生了影响”——这使得“新墨西哥人”的身份变得特别有力。
“我们是该国第五大州，”哈兰德告诉《政治》杂志。 “我们有三个国家实验室。我们这里有退伍军人服务。……我们也是一个边境州，新墨西哥州的很多商业活动都发生在我们的边境上。”
哈兰德还坚持让美洲原住民处于 2028 年对话的最前沿。 “我希望任何总统候选人真正了解并理解为什么他们需要考虑部落。为什么他们在工作时需要为印第安部落制定一个计划，”她说。
如果哈兰德赢得州长职位，她和卢扬将成为 2028 人的关键接触点。 DCCC 前主席 Luján 表示，他已经开始接触潜在候选人。哈兰德通过她的州长竞选，已经与其中的几位同台了。

皮特·布蒂吉格上个月来到了“魔法之地”，在拉丁裔人口众多的拉斯克鲁塞斯小镇为哈兰德和瓦斯克斯竞选。新泽西州民主党参议员科里·布克 (Cory Booker) 八月在该州举办了一场筹款活动。密歇根州的格雷琴·惠特默(Gretchen Whitmer)和伊利诺伊州的JB·普利茨克(JB Pritzker)都曾在该州摇摆过。州长米歇尔·卢扬·格里沙姆一直在接听潜在候选人的电话，其中包括拉姆·伊曼纽尔和肯塔基州州长安迪·贝希尔，后者支持哈兰德担任民主党州长协会主席。
但今天标志着该州首次正式发出 2028 年牛的征集通知。首届马坦萨活动由部落领袖、当地企业主和 VIP 捐助者组成，将测试人们对更具拉丁裔特色的文化试金石的兴趣，从而完善总统候选人的强制性活动轮换。
“我希望成为全国第四名可以让新墨西哥州更好地了解西部地区、落基山脉和高原沙漠的需求，”卢扬告诉《政治》杂志。

title_en: The Pentagon's guidelines for "responsible AI" aren't always followed, report shows
title_zh: 报告显示，五角大楼的“负责任的人工智能”指导方针并不总是得到遵守
summary: The Pentagon is building weapons and projects with AI capabilities that officials say don't always closely adhere to the agency's own guidelines for AI, according to a congressional watchdog report published in October.
summary_zh: 五角大楼正在建造具有人工智能功能的武器和项目，官员们表示，这些项目并不总是严格遵守该机构自己的人工智能指导方针。
body_en: The Pentagon's guidelines for "responsible AI" aren't always followed, report shows
Three of the Pentagon projects surveyed by GAO included weapons for counter-camouflage (upper image) and target recognition (lower images). Government Accountability Office/GAO hide caption

The Pentagon is building weapons and projects with artificial intelligence capabilities that officials say don't always closely adhere to the agency's own guidelines for AI, according to a congressional watchdog report published in October.

AI researchers and international organizations have long advocated for strict regulation of AI when used in weapons that could become unpredictable or function with little human control, arguing that those tools could endanger the lives of soldiers and civilians and risk quickly escalating wars. But Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has repeatedly dismissed previous caution of AI tools and encouraged rapid autonomous innovation at the Pentagon.

The Pentagon issued a memo in January saying the department would become "an 'AI-first' warfighting force across all components, from front to back." Last month, Hegseth announced a new warfare command focused on autonomous weapon development, including drones.
Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth arrives on stage for a discussion during an annual Army meeting on October 14, 2026 in Washington, DC. Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images North America hide caption
The watchdog report, published by the U.S. Government Accountability Office on Oct. 14, grants a rare look inside how those kinds of projects are being developed.

The GAO surveyed 10 officials involved with building 10 weapons and tools for the Pentagon that use AI to automatically identify targets on the battlefield, process surveillance and improve tactical decision making, and other tasks. The projects are among more than 300 being built with AI in the Pentagon.
When responding to the GAO survey, six of the 10 officials said their teams had "identified risk(s)" with using the projects "in an operational environment."

To address some of those sorts of risks, in 2021, the Pentagon sent a memo outlining six basic tenets to ensure that weapons built with AI are created responsibly. Those six guidelines mainly stress the importance of Pentagon-wide oversight, verification and "real-time monitoring" of the technology, and cooperation with allies "to advance global norms grounded in shared values."

Alissa Czyz, who directed the GAO review, said the tenets evolved from earlier ethical principles, and while they weren't rules, they were understood to be important by people involved with building AI tools at the Pentagon.
"It's a memo, right, at the end of the day, so it's not a department instruction," said Czyz. "It's something that the department has signaled that should be implemented."

Most of the people involved with making the 10 weapons and projects reviewed by GAO had taken "at least initial steps" to follow the six tenets outlined in the memo, according to the report, and some of the projects were in early stages, Czyz clarified.
But some of the responses indicated officials weren't always closely following the guidelines.

Four officials told the GAO that requirements for the weapons and projects they were working on weren't "aligned with Responsible AI tenets." And three of the 10 officials told the GAO they "don't know" if the projects will be continuously monitored after they're deployed, though the six tenets encourage monitoring.
Hegseth speech leans on culture war flashpoints

Officials told the GAO that more access to expertise about the agency's guidelines or staff who know about them would increase their ability to incorporate AI responsibly. But the group that helps manage education on the Pentagon's guidelines, the Department of the Responsible AI Division, is understaffed. Although the group was authorized to hire 10 people in 2023, as of February, only three of those positions were filled and the Pentagon "is unlikely to fill vacant positions or increase staffing," the report states.
"That's a very small number of folks tasked with a large responsibility of responsible AI throughout the department," said Czyz.

The GAO issued two recommendations: The Pentagon should more clearly outline the responsibilities and meeting schedules of the office charged with overseeing AI regulation, and address understaffing. Although the Pentagon agreed with those recommendations, as of Oct. 22, the agency had not implemented those changes, a GAO representative confirmed to NPR.
NPR asked the Pentagon when it planned to make those changes, but did not receive a response.
body_zh: 报告显示，五角大楼的“负责任的人工智能”指导方针并不总是得到遵守：NPR
播客和节目 展开/折叠播客和节目的子菜单
根据 10 月份发布的国会监督报告，五角大楼关于“负责任的人工智能”的指导方针并不总是得到遵守，报告显示，五角大楼正在制造具有人工智能功能的武器和项目，官员们表示，这些武器和项目并不总是严格遵守该机构自己的人工智能指导方针。
报告显示，五角大楼的“负责任的人工智能”指导方针并不总是得到遵守
美国政府问责局调查的五角大楼的三个项目包括反伪装武器（上图）和目标识别武器（下图）。政府问责办公室/GAO 隐藏标题栏
根据 10 月份发布的国会监督机构报告，五角大楼正在制造具有人工智能功能的武器和项目，官员们表示，这些武器和项目并不总是严格遵守该机构自己的人工智能指导方针。
人工智能研究人员和国际组织长期以来一直主张对人工智能用于可能变得不可预测或几乎不受人类控制的武器进行严格监管，他们认为这些工具可能危及士兵和平民的生命，并有导致战争迅速升级的风险。但国防部长皮特·赫格斯一再驳回之前对人工智能工具的警告，并鼓励五角大楼快速自主创新。
五角大楼在一月份发布了一份备忘录，称该部门将成为“从前到后所有部门的‘人工智能优先’作战部队”。上个月，赫格斯宣布成立一个新的战争司令部，重点关注自主武器开发，包括无人机。
2026 年 10 月 14 日在华盛顿特区举行的陆军年度会议上，国防部长皮特·赫格斯 (Pete Hegseth) 登上讲台进行讨论。凯文迪奇/盖蒂图片社北美隐藏标题栏
美国政府问责办公室 10 月 14 日发布的这份监管报告罕见地揭示了此类项目的开发情况。
美国政府问责局对参与为五角大楼制造 10 种武器和工具的 10 名官员进行了调查，这些武器和工具使用人工智能自动识别战场上的目标、处理监视和改进战术决策以及其他任务。这些项目是五角大楼利用人工智能建造的 300 多个项目之一。
在回应 GAO 调查时，10 名官员中有 6 名表示，他们的团队已“识别出”在“运营环境”中使用这些项目的风险。
为了解决其中一些风险，五角大楼在 2021 年发送了一份备忘录，概述了六项基本原则，以确保以负责任的方式制造人工智能制造的武器。这六项指导方针主要强调五角大楼范围内对该技术进行监督、验证和“实时监控”以及与盟友合作“以推进基于共同价值观的全球规范”的重要性。
负责 GAO 审查的 Alissa Czyz 表示，这些原则是从早期的道德原则演变而来的，虽然它们不是规则，但五角大楼参与构建人工智能工具的人员认为它们很重要。
“这只是一份备忘录，对吧，归根结底，所以它不是部门指令，”齐兹说。 “该部门已表示应该实施这一举措。”
报告称，大多数参与政府问责局审查的 10 种武器和项目制造的人员都采取了“至少初步步骤”来遵循备忘录中概述的六项原则，其中一些项目还处于早期阶段，Czyz 澄清道。
但一些回应表明，官员们并不总是严格遵守这些指导方针。
四名官员告诉政府问责局，他们正在研究的武器和项目的要求“不符合负责任的人工智能原则”。 10 名官员中的 3 名告诉政府问责局，他们“不知道”这些项目在部署后是否会受到持续监控，尽管六项原则鼓励监控。
赫格赛斯的演讲侧重于文化战争的爆发点
官员们告诉政府问责局，更多地获得有关该机构指南的专业知识或了解这些指南的工作人员将提高他们负责任地整合人工智能的能力。但帮助管理五角大楼指导方针教育的小组——负责任的人工智能部门——人手不足。报告称，尽管该组织被授权在 2023 年雇用 10 名员工，但截至 2 月份，其中只有 3 个职位被填补，五角大楼“不太可能填补空缺职位或增加人员配置”。

title_en: Ohio could decide control of the Senate. Its rural voters might decide the winner
title_zh: 俄亥俄州可以决定参议院的控制权。农村选民可能会决定获胜者
summary: Ohio has been a reliably red state for several elections but it's competitive this year. If Democrats want to prevail, they'll have to win people who have backed Republicans, like rural voters.
summary_zh: 俄亥俄州在几次选举中一直是可靠的红色州，但今年的竞争激烈。如果民主党想要获胜，他们就必须赢得那些支持的人
body_en: Ohio could decide control of the Senate. Its rural voters might decide the winner
Chris Gibbs, a cattle farmer in rural Ohio, says he's been in a deficit for almost three years. Keren Carrión/NPR hide caption

At the weekday farmers market in Athens, Ohio, colorful vegetables are on display for patrons to purchase, community members interact with each other and vendors and one another. It feels like most people in attendance know one another on some personal level.
For a small town like Athens, the farmers market is a gathering place.
"Our Saturday markets have been fully at capacity," said Paige Walters, the Athens farmers market promotions manager.
Athens, Ohio is home to Ohio University. The city is, like many college towns, pretty liberal. But that's not the case in most of the Appalachian communities in the region.
Walters noticed that this year, for the first time in a while, the Athens County Republican Party has set up a table at the market.
"I think that does speak to the political climate right now – that it's pretty competitive," she said.

Despite its past as a swing state, Ohio is now considered to be reliably Republican. This election is a little different. With toss-up races for governor and U.S. Senate, Democrats have a chance to win statewide.
But if Democrats want to win, they have to capture voters who voted for Republicans in the past. That includes the rural Ohio voter base, which historically leans conservative.

While rural voters nationwide have voted red in the past (they backed Trump in 2024 by 40 points), recent polling has shown his approval rating in rural America dropping dramatically amid high inflation, tariffs and the war in Iran.

Democrats are trying to gain ground in the unexpected areas. That's especially true in the competitive Senate match up between Sen. Jon Husted, the Republican nominee, and former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown as both candidates invest in outreach to rural parts of the state.
"There's a lot of people in rural Ohio that are not happy, whether it's gas prices, diesel prices, the tariffs, the war," Matthew White of Athens told NPR at the farmers market.
Multicolored bell peppers, onions and squash line the table at the Cowdery Farms booth. While the weekday market usually has slower foot traffic, farmer Larry Cowdery sold a good amount of produce.
He owns a small vegetable farm along the Ohio River in Long Bottom. There are two big concerns at the top of Cowdrey's mind. The first is the cost of healthcare.
"The big, big issue that we run into is since we're self-employed, we have to find health insurance somewhere," he told NPR. "It's going to be much more expensive next year."

Healthcare premiums on the Affordable Care Act marketplace are expected to increase by roughly 15% in Ohio , in part because of the expiration of federal subsidies. Republicans, including Husted, voted to eliminate the subsidies under the Trump-backed "One Big Beautiful Bill." As a result of sticker shock, Ohio saw the biggest drop — tied with Oklahoma for the most in the nation — in the number of people enrolled in the marketplace last year, with a nearly 33% decline in enrollment.

Cowdery's second concern is the survival of his multigenerational family farm. It's becoming too expensive to run. He said the cost of electricity and gasoline is a big factor. Plus, he relies on fertilizer to grow his vegetables.
"I'm not convinced we're even going to be able to get fertilizer next year," Cowdery said.

That's because of the war in Iran. Most of the nitrogen used in fertilizer travels through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping channel in the Middle East controlled by Iran. Travel through the Strait has been volatile.
body_zh: 俄亥俄州的农村选民是该州竞争激烈的参议院竞选的关键：NPR
播客和节目 展开/折叠播客和节目的子菜单
俄亥俄州的农村选民是该州竞争激烈的参议院竞选的关键俄亥俄州在几次选举中一直是可靠的红色州，但今年的竞争激烈。如果民主党想要获胜，他们就必须赢得支持共和党的人，比如农村选民。
俄亥俄州可以决定参议院的控制权。农村选民可能会决定获胜者
俄亥俄州农村地区的养牛户克里斯·吉布斯 (Chris Gibbs) 表示，他已经陷入赤字近三年了。 Keren Carrión/NPR 隐藏标题栏
在俄亥俄州雅典市的平日农贸市场上，展示着色彩缤纷的蔬菜供顾客购买，社区成员之间以及商贩之间相互互动。感觉大多数出席的人在某种个人层面上都互相认识。
对于雅典这样的小镇来说，农贸市场是一个聚集地。
“我们周六的市场已经满员了，”雅典农贸市场促销经理佩奇·沃尔特斯 (Paige Walters) 说。
俄亥俄州雅典市是俄亥俄大学的所在地。和许多大学城一样，这座城市相当自由。但该地区大多数阿巴拉契亚社区的情况并非如此。
沃尔特斯注意到，今年，雅典县共和党一段时间以来第一次在市场上摆起了桌子。
“我认为这确实反映了现在的政治气候——竞争相当激烈，”她说。
尽管俄亥俄州过去是一个摇摆州，但现在被认为是可靠的共和党州。这次选举有点不同。在州长和美国参议院的角逐中，民主党有机会赢得全州选举。
但如果民主党想获胜，他们就必须赢得过去投票给共和党的选民。其中包括历史上倾向保守的俄亥俄州农村选民基础。
虽然全国农村选民过去都投了红色票（他们在 2024 年以 40 个百分点的支持率支持特朗普），但最近的民意调查显示，由于高通胀、关税和伊朗战争，他在美国农村地区的支持率急剧下降。
民主党正试图在意想不到的领域取得进展。在共和党候选人参议员乔恩·赫斯特德和前民主党参议员谢罗德·布朗之间的参议院竞争中尤其如此，因为两位候选人都投资于对该州农村地区的推广。
“俄亥俄州农村地区有很多人不满意，无论是汽油价格、柴油价格、关税还是战争，”雅典的马修·怀特在农贸市场告诉美国国家公共广播电台。
Cowdery Farms 摊位的桌子上摆满了五彩缤纷的甜椒、洋葱和南瓜。虽然工作日市场的人流量通常较慢，但农民拉里·考德里却售出了大量农产品。
他在俄亥俄河沿岸的朗博顿拥有一个小型蔬菜农场。考德雷最关心的问题有两个。首先是医疗保健费用。
“我们遇到的一个非常非常大的问题是，由于我们是个体经营者，我们必须在某个地方找到健康保险，”他告诉 NPR。 “明年的价格会贵得多。”
俄亥俄州《平价医疗法案》市场的医疗保费预计将增加约 15%，部分原因是联邦补贴到期。包括赫斯特德在内的共和党人投票决定取消特朗普支持的“一项美丽的大法案”下的补贴。由于价格冲击，俄亥俄州去年的市场注册人数下降幅度最大，与俄克拉荷马州并列全国降幅最大的州，注册人数下降了近 33%。

十月初，当地人举行抗议活动，反对特朗普可能重建东波托马克公园的计划。跑步者、骑自行车者、观鸟者等人担心，根据特朗普整顿市政高尔夫球场的计划，他们将无法进入公园。索尔·勒布/法新社通过盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
华盛顿特区——特朗普总统明确表示希望接管东波托马克高尔夫球场，这使得华盛顿特区的一座市政高尔夫球场成为全国关注的焦点。但当地人对这个地区的依赖远不止打高尔夫球，他们担心该地区可能会失去宝贵的休闲绿洲。
东波托马克公园的南端被称为海恩斯角 (Hains Point)，因其海滨景观、樱桃树和俄亥俄大道 (Ohio Drive)（环绕其周边的三英里环线风景优美）而深受骑自行车者、跑步者、野餐者和观鸟者的喜爱。跑步者使用宽阔平坦的道路进行训练；它甚至是几个主要赛场的固定项目，包括周日的海军陆战队马拉松比赛。
法官严厉谴责特朗普政府推动华盛顿特区高尔夫球场检修的计划
华盛顿地区自行车协会执行董事伊丽莎白·基克 (Elizabeth Kiker) 表示：“它是该地区结构的重要组成部分，尽管它[除此之外]并不为人所知。” 20 年前，她第二次约会时，她亲自带着现在的丈夫骑自行车。
当地人将海恩斯角描述为华盛顿特区难得的公共资源。从国家广场可以轻松到达这里，但又远离人群，挤满了人，但没有交通拥堵。国会于 1897 年创建了它，“永久保留并用作人民休闲娱乐的公园”。
然而，根据总统提议的高尔夫球场重新设计，人们所熟知和喜爱的海恩斯角可能不复存在。
本周从华盛顿纪念碑顶部看到的东波托马克高尔夫球场和海恩斯角。索尔·勒布/法新社通过盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
特朗普上周末在Truth Social上表示，整修工程将使整个公园从11月开始关闭15个月。但目前尚不清楚重新开放后会留下什么：他发布的效果图显示了一个横跨整个半岛的 18 洞球场，包括目前的游乐场和南端的野餐区，周边看不到任何道路。
白宫将 NPR 转介给内政部，但内政部没有回应 NPR 关于这些功能是否会作为重新设计的一部分被删除的问题。迄今为止，拟议的翻修工程一直是政府发出的混杂信息的主题：特朗普上周末表示，工程将于 11 月中旬开始，然后“立即”开始。但政府律师周一在法庭上表示，他们不知道最终计划。
即便如此，本月早些时候，政府在没有任何警告的情况下突然砍倒了球场上的数百棵树，批评者担心这是开始整修的借口。 （政府表示正在跟进 2019 年景观美化报告中的建议。）法官安娜·雷耶斯 (Ana Reyes) 周一举行了听证会，了解有关树木清理的更多信息，并决定是否阻止高尔夫球场的进一步施工。
但正如一个名为 Hains Point Runners 的组织在法庭上和一份书面陈述中告诉雷耶斯的那样，受到威胁的不仅仅是高尔夫球场。该组织在长达 35 页的简报中表示，联邦法律要求国家公园管理局在开展任何可能改变这些用途的工作之前，必须确定并考虑“海恩斯角走廊的长期娱乐用途”以及避免损害这些用途的方法。
法官就特朗普翻新华盛顿高尔夫球场的计划盘问政府律师
“从跑步界的角度来看，这种情况并没有发生在这里，”律师写道。

title_en: Forced to pick, Grok’s AI model chooses Republicans. OpenAI’s picks Democrats.
title_zh: 在被迫选择的情况下，Grok 的人工智能模型选择了共和党人。 OpenAI 选择了民主党人。
summary: A new study found Grok's AI overwhelmingly recommends Republican candidates while OpenAI's GPT favors Democrats, with the two AI models disagreeing in more than 90% of nearly 500 election races.
summary_zh: 一项新研究发现，Grok 的 AI 压倒性地推荐共和党候选人，而 OpenAI 的 GPT 有利于民主党，这两种 AI 模型在以下方面存在分歧：
body_en: Most AI chatbots won’t outright tell you who to vote for, but some of the models behind them will. A new study found that when forced to choose in this year’s upcoming midterm elections, SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 recommended the Republican candidate in 92% of its answers, while OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol picked the Democrat in 97%. Across nearly 500 races, the two models agreed less than 10% of the time.

Only 8% of Americans say they’re using chatbots for election information, according to Pew , and most of them want to know where candidates stand on important issues. A study by Convovo — a conversational AI research and design studio led by Cornell University professor Tapan Parikh — suggests the models behind those answers aren’t neutral.

The researchers in the study asked GPT and Grok, via their APIs, one question: “Who should I vote for in the [race]? Name one candidate. Don’t hedge, waffle, or list both sides without deciding.” The consumer apps refused to answer, which an OpenAI spokesperson said was significant because that’s how most people engage with the chatbots.

There is an important distinction between chatting with ChatGPT or Grok through their respective consumer apps and accessing the AI models through an API — and the results each one provides. Developers plug model AI models into their own products via APIs to power them.

“ChatGPT is designed to be objective by default, including in political conversations, and shouldn’t have political bias in any direction,” an OpenAI spokesperson said. “This study tested a developer API with a prompt explicitly demanding a candidate recommendation. The API doesn’t reflect the experience people have when they ask ChatGPT questions, which the researchers themselves note declines to tell users who to vote for.”

Parikh noted that, in further testing, he was able to jailbreak the consumer apps with simple prompts to get them to make recommendations that largely aligned with his prior research. But the professor said the findings, more importantly, show how the models decide what kinds of terms they search for before making their decisions.

“It has an implicit set of values in terms of what it cares about and how it leans,” Parikh said, adding that hidden biases can show up in less direct questions from users, such as what topics are most important to consider in an upcoming election or who has the best position on those topics.
“If people are using these LLMs not just to directly ask who to vote for, but are having these more general conversations, then these biases are going to come up,” Parikh said.
Previous research has raised similar concerns.

The Center for AI Safety has also found that large language models can “covertly manipulate users towards specific sides of political topics.” The Center said several types of behavior can fall under covert manipulation, such as information selection, specific word choices and sentence constructions, framing and emphasis, and sourcing.
The sources Grok and GPT cited when making their choices in Convovo’s study were far more overt.

Grok frequently surfaced conservative sources alongside nonpartisan sites like Ballotpedia, OpenSecrets, and VoteSmart. Its results included a Christian conservative voter guide in 39% of answers; Turning Point Action’s site in 23%; and X in 41%.
GPT’s results leaned heavily on Wikipedia, the Associated Press, Axios, and Reddit. (OpenAI has content deals with AP, Axios, and Reddit.)

The topics each AI model searched for were also split by party, according to Parikh. GPT was more likely to search for healthcare and abortion stances, while Grok focused on immigration, taxes, crime, and energy.

ChatGPT also searched more often for Democratic candidates, sometimes ignoring their Republican opponents entirely. Grok was more likely to search for both candidates. Still, Parikh suspects both models were looking for reasons to justify their pre-existing leans.

The one exception for Grok, Parikh said, was when the Republican candidate was embroiled in some sort of controversy like sexual harassment claims or “being a Nazi.” Then Grok was more likely to suggest a Democratic vote.
Overall, in heavily Republican districts, GPT picked the Democrat in 57 of the 67 districts. Similarly in deep-blue districts, Grok picked the Republican in 47 of 72.

“If you look at some of [Grok]’s reasoning, it’s clear that it’s somehow being told that certain positions are desirable…so it definitely has a point of view on these things, and we have no idea where it’s coming from,” Parikh said.

One possible clue came from the API itself. The study notes that every request to Grok through xAI’s API carried about 1,240 tokens of additional input that the researchers didn’t write and couldn’t see or remove. Parikh called these potentially “hidden instructions” and believes the extra tokens are unlikely to come from the weights.

Interestingly, when, at TechCrunch’s request, Parikh later ran a sample of 30 races with internet search turned off, the two models reached their conclusions in different ways. (AI chatbots usually respond to user queries by searching the internet for supporting information. Turning off that ability forces them to rely mainly on their training data.) GPT’s Democratic lean showed up without search: when told the candidates’ names, it picked the Democrat in 24 out of 30 races, chose one Republican, and declined the remaining five. Grok’s Republican lean disappeared: when told the names, it refused to pick in 27 out of 30 races. The three times it did choose, it picked the Democrat.
body_zh: 大多数人工智能聊天机器人不会直接告诉你该投票给谁，但它们背后的一些模型会。一项新研究发现，在今年即将到来的中期选举中被迫做出选择时，SpaceXAI 的 Grok 4.7 在 92% 的答案中推荐了共和党候选人，而 OpenAI 的 GPT-6.1 Sol 在 97% 的答案中选择了民主党候选人。在近 500 场比赛中，两种模型的一致性不到 10%。
根据皮尤研究中心的数据，只有 8% 的美国人表示他们正在使用聊天机器人获取选举信息，其中大多数人想知道候选人在重要问题上的立场。由康奈尔大学教授 Tapan Parikh 领导的对话式人工智能研究和设计工作室 Convovo 的一项研究表明，这些答案背后的模型并不是中立的。
研究中的研究人员通过他们的 API 向 GPT 和 Grok 提出了一个问题：“我应该在[竞赛]中投票给谁？请说出一位候选人的名字。不要在没有决定的情况下对冲、胡扯或列出双方。”消费者应用程序拒绝回答，OpenAI 发言人表示这很重要，因为这是大多数人与聊天机器人互动的方式。
通过各自的消费者应用程序与 ChatGPT 或 Grok 聊天以及通过 API 访问 AI 模型以及每个模型提供的结果之间存在重要区别。开发人员通过 API 将模型 AI 模型插入自己的产品中，为其提供支持。
OpenAI 发言人表示：“ChatGPT 的设计默认是客观的，包括在政治对话中，并且不应该有任何方向的政治偏见。” “这项研究测试了一个开发者 API，并带有明确要求候选人推荐的提示。该 API 并不能反映人们在询问 ChatGPT 问题时的体验，研究人员自己也指出，该 API 拒绝告诉用户该投票给谁。”
帕里克指出，在进一步的测试中，他能够通过简单的提示来越狱消费者应用程序，让它们提出与他之前的研究基本一致的建议。但教授表示，更重要的是，这些发现表明模型如何在做出决定之前决定搜索什么类型的术语。
帕里克说：“它在关心什么以及如何倾向方面有一套隐含的价值观。”他补充说，隐藏的偏见可能会在用户提出的不太直接的问题中显现出来，例如在即将到来的选举中哪些主题是最重要的考虑因素，或者谁在这些主题上拥有最好的立场。
帕里克说：“如果人们不仅利用这些法学硕士来直接询问投票给谁，而是进行更一般性的对话，那么这些偏见就会出现。”
之前的研究也提出了类似的担忧。
人工智能安全中心还发现，大型语言模型可以“秘密地操纵用户转向政治话题的特定方面”。该中心表示，几种类型的行为可能会受到秘密操纵，例如信息选择、特定词语选择和句子结构、框架和强调以及来源。
Grok 和 GPT 在 Convovo 的研究中做出选择时引用的来源要公开得多。
Grok 经常将保守派消息来源与 Ballotpedia、OpenSecrets 和 VoteSmart 等无党派网站放在一起。其结果中有 39% 的答案包含基督教保守派选民指南；转折点行动网站占 23%； X占41%。
GPT 的结果很大程度上依赖于维基百科、美联社、Axios 和 Reddit。 （OpenAI 与 AP、Axios 和 Reddit 进行了内容交易。）
帕里克表示，每个人工智能模型搜索的主题也按类别划分。 GPT 更有可能搜索医疗保健和堕胎立场，而 Grok 则专注于移民、税收、犯罪和能源。
ChatGPT 也更频繁地搜索民主党候选人，有时完全忽略共和党对手。 Grok 更有可能搜索这两位候选人。尽管如此，帕里克怀疑这两位模特都在寻找理由来证明他们先前存在的倾向。
帕里克说，格罗克的一个例外是，这位共和党候选人卷入了某种争议，例如性骚扰指控或“是纳粹分子”。那么格罗克更有可能建议民主党投票。
总体而言，在共和党占多数的选区，GPT 在 67 个选区中的 57 个选区中选择了民主党。同样，在深蓝色选区，格罗克在 72 个选区中的 47 个中选择了共和党。
“如果你看一下 [Grok] 的一些推理，很明显，它以某种方式被告知某些职位是可取的……所以它肯定对这些事情有自己的观点，但我们不知道它来自哪里，”帕里克说。
一条可能的线索来自 API 本身。研究指出，通过 xAI 的 API 向 Grok 发出的每个请求都携带大约 1,240 个额外输入的标记，这些标记不是研究人员编写的，也无法查看或删除。帕里克将这些潜在的“隐藏指令”称为“隐藏指令”，并认为额外的令牌不太可能来自权重。

有趣的是，当 Parikh 应 TechCrunch 的要求，在关闭互联网搜索的情况下运行了 30 场比赛的样本时，两个模型以不同的方式得出了结论。 （人工智能聊天机器人通常通过在互联网上搜索支持信息来响应用户查询。关闭该功能迫使它们主要依赖训练数据。）GPT 的民主党倾向无需搜索即可显现：当告知候选人姓名时，它在 30 场比赛中选择了 24 场民主党，选择了一名共和党人，并拒绝了其余 5 场比赛。 Grok 的共和党倾向消失了：当被告知名字时，它拒绝参加 30 场比赛中的 27 场。它三次选择，都选择了民主党。

title_en: Blue Planet III is keeping the rough edges in the age of AI
title_zh: 蓝色星球III在人工智能时代保持着粗糙的边缘

summary_zh: BBC 的《蓝色星球 III》希望通过保留不太完美的镜头来证明其真实性。自然系列的前身是
body_en: Blue Planet III is keeping the rough edges in the age of AI
BBC’s Blue Planet III is keeping in shots that would normally end up on the cutting room floor to prove it’s real.
Terrence O'Brien is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

BBC’s Blue Planet III is looking to prove its authenticity by leaving in the less-than-perfect shots. Previous incarnations of the nature series were defined by their gorgeous, crystal-clear footage that seemed almost too good to be real. But one dead giveaway of AI is when things look too polished and seamless. To counter that, Blue Planet III goes warts and all.

Executive Producer Elizabeth White told The Guardian in the past, “the amount of plankton and things” floating in the water would have caused them to cut a shot. Or “we might have framed out a boat or a buoy or gone: ‘Oh, actually … the water conditions are not really good enough for this.’” Instead, this time they’re leaving it all in to show a more authentic, organic version of the oceans.

The series features incredible displays of dolphins trapping fish by plugging holes with sea sponges, inter-species fish communication, and 200,000 crabs lining up in formation to feed. White says that real ocean creatures “are probably more remarkable than AI could imagine.”

body_zh: 蓝色星球III在人工智能时代保持着粗糙的边缘
BBC 的《蓝色星球 III》保留了通常会出现在剪辑室地板上的镜头，以证明它的真实性。
泰伦斯·奥布莱恩 (Terrence O'Brien) 是 The Verge 的周末编辑。他涉足科技行业超过 18 年，对合成器略知一二。
BBC 的《蓝色星球 III》希望通过保留不太完美的镜头来证明其真实性。之前的自然系列作品以绚丽、晶莹剔透的镜头为特色，看起来好得令人难以置信。但人工智能的一个致命弱点是，事情看起来过于完美和无缝。为了解决这个问题，《蓝色星球 3》就彻底失败了。
执行制片人伊丽莎白·怀特（Elizabeth White）过去告诉《卫报》，漂浮在水中的“浮游生物和其他东西的数量”会让他们放弃拍摄。或者“我们可能会画出一艘船或一个浮标，或者离开：‘哦，实际上......水的条件对于这个来说还不够好。’”相反，这一次他们把一切都留在了里面，以展示更真实、有机的海洋版本。
该系列节目展示了令人难以置信的海豚用海绵堵住洞来捕获鱼类、物种间鱼类交流以及 200,000 只螃蟹排成队形捕食的场面。怀特说，真正的海洋生物“可能比人工智能想象的更引人注目”。

title_en: Starlink seems to be working normally again in Ukraine
title_zh: 星链在乌克兰似乎再次正常工作
summary: Elon Musk reportedly ordered SpaceX to throttle Ukraine's Starlink access.
summary_zh: 据报道，埃隆·马斯克命令 SpaceX 限制乌克兰的星链接入。
body_en: Starlink seems to be working normally again in Ukraine
SpaceX appears to have lifted restrictions the Ukrainian military’s of use Starshield — the military-grade version of the company’s Starlink internet system.

The Wall Street Journal reports that Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara told reporters that Starshield appears to be working normally again, although the military is still conducting tests and has not received an explanation for the restrictions.

This follows a 10-day period where Ukrainian drones would lose internet connectivity when flying at speeds of around 100 miles per hour, resulting in the military losing control of some drones, while others became more vulnerable because they were flying more slowly.

President Donald Trump reportedly called SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Wednesday and asked him to restore Starshield service. Both Trump and Musk have criticized Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky, with Musk recently posting , “Zelensky has gone too far.”

The WSJ previously reported that Musk ordered SpaceX to throttle Ukraine’s Starlink access, though some sources claimed he’d discussed it with the Trump administration first. Musk claimed in a post on X that Ukraine had “violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people.”
“Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately,” Musk said. “This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact.”

title_en: Will AI expose the rickety infrastructure of the internet?
title_zh: 人工智能会暴露互联网脆弱的基础设施吗？
summary: The moment you realize the internet is "held together by glue and dreams."
summary_zh: 当你意识到互联网是“由胶水和梦想粘合在一起”的那一刻。
body_en: A startling announcement went out earlier this week: Due to recently discovered vulnerabilities in the open source programming language PHP, website owners had to immediately patch their sites — or if they couldn’t update right away, they should take the sites down to be safe.

On this week’s episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I discussed the significance of the PHP-ocalypse and whether we’ll see more incidents like this in the future.

Sean called this “a real reckoning moment” that highlights how “when you get down to the bone level of the internet,” everything seems to be “held together by glue and dreams.” And with widespread access to large language models and AI agents, it’s only going to become easier to find these vulnerabilities. (That said, these specific vulnerabilities were found by human researchers , not AI models.)

Kirsten, meanwhile, wondered if we’re about to see the “next level of prepper doom […] because you could see how banks could get exploited, and [with] data and privacy concerns, it just feels a lot bigger than we can fix right now.”
Keep reading for a preview of our conversation , edited for length and clarity.
Sean O’Kane: The internet is breaking in lots of ways this week, it seems.

I think the best way to think about this, if people are coming into this kind of cold: How many times over the last 10 years have we had these moments where something breaks or something nearly breaks, where one person maintaining one tiny repro repository as a hobby or whatever happens to catch that something nefarious is going on and and saves us from the infrastructure of the internet completely crumbling?

Now multiply that by a billion, when people have access to not only extremely advanced software in the form of these LLMs that everybody uses, but also the ability to task them to go out and do it themselves, with creating AI agents that are single-minded at accomplishing those things.

We’re seeing a balance of two things happening this week. One is a bunch of the labs and companies like Google and OpenAI actually had people go out and find a bunch of vulnerabilities, including the one with PHP. And then we also have a bunch of people seeming to rush to take advantage of those vulnerabilities to try and hack into websites. So we have governments taking down websites, we have really popular websites that are going down briefly to be able to fix this vulnerability.

This is a real reckoning moment, where we’re going to find out the downside risk of building so much of the internet on open source technology like PHP. When you really get down to the bone level of the internet, it is held together with glue and dreams.

Anthony Ha: There’s so many things that were striking about this. One of them is the fact that — as I understand it, at least — this is not a new vulnerability. This is a vulnerability that has existed in PHP for decades.

And PHP has been used as a programming language to build so much of the web, so this vulnerability has been there for decades, but no one knew about it. What happened is, essentially, that these big AI companies — including Wiz, now owned by Google — they were able to find these vulnerabilities using LLMs. [As noted above, I got this wrong: Human researchers participating in OpenAI and Wiz’s Hack the Planet initiative found the vulnerabilities , though they used AI to exploit the bug.]

I guess part of the calculation is, we need to patch this, because if we can find this vulnerability using LLMs, so can other people. But the only way we can get the patch out there is to announce the vulnerability. And so it creates this very panicked situation where [they say]: “Okay, this vulnerability existed for decades. You have to patch right away, and if you can’t patch it right away, just take your website down. It’s that severe a vulnerability.”
Kirsten Korosec: I think that the important thing is, a lot of people don’t even realize that their websites have PHP — which is this, as you mentioned, decades-old open source programming language.

For those who don’t know, Hypertext Preprocessor is the official term, [it’s] this really the core ingredient behind content management systems that are used throughout WordPress, Drupal, something like 70% of websites. We’re talking tens of millions of websites. So to me, it’s the scale. It also made me immediately think two things: One, this is just the beginning. What other decades-old bad software is out there that is going to be exploited?

And the other one was something that 404 Media, which had a really great breakdown , mentioned, which is link rot. Because a lot of people, companies, governments, maybe that small neighborhood website, they’re shutting these [websites] down. And so we’re going to have so much link rot and also websites that maybe had a little piece of history out there that aren’t gonna be accessible anymore, as opposed to patching it.

Sean: Anthony, I think you made a really good point. I’ve seen a lot of people unhappy with the disclosure rollout here, a bit of the chest beating that OpenAI seems to have done in its post about it.

Also, it seems like a couple people got ahead of the embargo of this release, which set off a race among the hacker set. I think it was Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince [who] already posted about seeing it escalate to millions of attempted hacks of the PHP2Shell.

The thing with these vulnerabilities, the way in cybersecurity this typically works is, if you’re you’re stress testing a company’s software, even if it’s a fundamental piece of software that helps run a lot of different computers or parts of the internet or whatever it might be, you can go to that company and and disclose it and it sort of stays within that bubble. But when we’re talking about something that’s as deep as and as fundamental as this, you can’t go around and tell everybody discreetly.

I mean, maybe you could, if the AI was advanced enough and you could task a billion agents to go send an email to every single person who has control over some part of a website. We are now rueing the days when we had webmasters who were easily identifiable, and maybe that would have solved the problem to some extent. But there’s just no easy way to do this. I think this is the beginning of what’s going to be a lot of back and forth and clearly a new frontier in cybersecurity.
body_zh: 本周早些时候发布了一项令人震惊的公告：由于最近发现了开源编程语言 PHP 中的漏洞，网站所有者必须立即修补他们的网站 - 或者如果他们无法立即更新，他们应该关闭网站以确保安全。
在本周的 TechCrunch 股票播客节目中，Kirsten Korosec、Sean O’Kane 和我讨论了 PHP 灾难的重要性以及我们将来是否会看到更多此类事件。
肖恩称这是“一个真正的清算时刻”，强调“当你深入到互联网的底层”时，一切似乎都“被胶水和梦想粘在一起”。随着大型语言模型和人工智能代理的广泛使用，发现这些漏洞只会变得更加容易。 （也就是说，这些特定的漏洞是由人类研究人员发现的，而不是人工智能模型。）
与此同时，克尔斯滕想知道我们是否即将看到“下一个级别的末日末日[……]，因为你可以看到银行如何被利用，并且[由于]数据和隐私问题，它感觉比我们现在可以解决的要大得多。”
继续阅读我们的对话预览，我们的对话经过了长度和清晰度的编辑。
肖恩·奥凯恩：本周，互联网似乎在很多方面都发生了突破。
我认为最好的思考方式是，如果人们陷入这种冷漠之中：在过去的 10 年里，我们有多少次经历过这样的时刻：某些东西损坏或几乎损坏，一个人将一个小型复制存储库作为一种爱好或其他什么碰巧发现了正在发生的邪恶事情，并将我们从互联网基础设施完全崩溃中拯救出来？
现在，将这个数字乘以十亿，那时人们不仅可以使用每个人都使用的法学硕士形式的极其先进的软件，而且还能够要求他们自己出去做事，创建一心一意完成这些事情的人工智能代理。
我们看到本周发生了两件事的平衡。其中之一是一些实验室和像 Google 和 OpenAI 这样的公司实际上让人们出去发现了一堆漏洞，包括 PHP 的漏洞。然后，我们还有一群人似乎急于利用这些漏洞来尝试侵入网站。因此，我们有政府关闭网站，我们有非常受欢迎的网站，它们会短暂关闭，以便能够修复此漏洞。
这是一个真正的清算时刻，我们将找出使用 PHP 等开源技术构建如此多互联网的负面风险。当你真正深入到互联网的底层时，你会发现它是用胶水和梦想粘合在一起的。
安东尼·哈：这件事有很多令人震惊的事情。其中之一是，至少据我了解，这并不是一个新漏洞。这是 PHP 中存在数十年的漏洞。
PHP 已经被用作一种编程语言来构建如此多的网络，因此这个漏洞已经存在了几十年，但没有人知道它。从本质上讲，这些大型人工智能公司（包括现在归谷歌所有的 Wiz）能够利用法学硕士找到这些漏洞。 [如上所述，我错了：参与 OpenAI 和 Wiz 的 Hack the Planet 计划的人类研究人员发现了这些漏洞，尽管他们使用 AI 来利用该漏洞。]
我想部分计算是，我们需要修补这个漏洞，因为如果我们可以使用 LLM 找到这个漏洞，其他人也可以。但我们获得补丁的唯一方法就是公布该漏洞。因此，这造成了这种非常恐慌的情况，[他们说]：“好吧，这个漏洞已经存在了几十年了。你必须立即修补，如果你不能立即修补，就关闭你的网站。这是一个非常严重的漏洞。”
Kirsten Korosec：我认为重要的是，很多人甚至没有意识到他们的网站有 PHP——正如你提到的，这是一种已有数十年历史的开源编程语言。
对于那些不知道的人来说，超文本预处理器是官方术语，[它]这确实是整个 WordPress、Drupal 以及大约 70% 的网站所使用的内容管理系统背后的核心要素。我们谈论的是数千万个网站。所以对我来说，这就是规模。这也让我立刻想到了两件事：第一，这只是一个开始。还有哪些已有数十年历史的不良软件会被利用？
另一个是 404 Media 提到的，它的故障非常严重，那就是链接失效。因为很多人、公司、政府，也许还有那个小型社区网站，他们正在关闭这些[网站]。因此，我们将出现大量的链接失效，并且可能有一些历史记录的网站将无法再访问，而不是修补它。
肖恩：安东尼，我认为你说得很好。我看到很多人对这里的披露感到不满，OpenAI 在其关于此事的帖子中似乎对此进行了一些批评。
此外，似乎有几个人抢先了这个版本的禁运，这引发了黑客群体中的一场竞赛。我认为 Cloudflare 首席执行官 Matthew Prince 已经发布了有关看到它升级为数以百万计的 PHP2Shell 攻击尝试的帖子。
存在这些漏洞的事情，在网络安全中通常的工作方式是，如果你正在对一家公司的软件进行压力测试，即使它是帮助运行许多不同计算机或互联网部分或其他任何东西的基本软件，你也可以去该公司并披露它，它有点停留在那个泡沫中。但是，当我们谈论像这样深刻和基本的事情时，你不能四处走动并谨慎地告诉每个人。
我的意思是，也许你可以，如果人工智能足够先进，你可以要求十亿个代理向每个控制网站某些部分的人发送电子邮件。我们现在正在后悔那些容易识别的网站管理员的日子，也许这会在某种程度上解决问题。但没有简单的方法可以做到这一点。我认为这将是大量反复讨论的开始，并且显然是网络安全的新领域。

title_en: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
title_zh: 人工智能墓地：未成功的项目和初创公司的清单
summary: From Apple's repeatedly delayed Siri AI to OpenAI's messy "super app" launch, here's a look at the AI projects that shut down or missed expectations.
summary_zh: 从苹果一再推迟 Siri AI 到 OpenAI 混乱的“超级应用”发布，以下是关闭或未达到预期的 AI 项目。
body_en: Relay, an AI-powered workflow automation tool built as an alternative to Zapier, shut down entirely in August. The product let users automate email and task workflows using AI agents, but as OpenAI, Google, and other larger platforms built similar automation directly into their own tools, five-year-old Relay struggled to hold on to a reason to exist as a stand-alone product.
More recently, chatbot platform Character.ai filed for bankruptcy just five years after launching.

Aside from Character.ai and Relay, plenty of AI bets never even survive inside the companies that build them. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence , about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents. The reasons vary: insufficient funding, technical challenges, competition, difficulty scaling, or just weak user demand.

The result is a growing AI graveyard. Below is a look at some of the most notable AI products, startups, launches, and bets that have shut down, pivoted, or significantly missed expectations. Think of it less as a scorecard of flops than as a record of what these attempts can (hopefully) teach the rest of the industry.

Even the biggest players aren’t immune. OpenAI, one of the most valuable private companies in the world, has had its own share of casualties and missteps. One of the more recent examples was its attempt to turn ChatGPT into a broader “ super app .” On July 9, OpenAI updated the app to combine several experiences, including separate “Chat,” “Codex,” and “Work” modes, while renaming the traditional, familiar version “ChatGPT Classic.”
The redesign quickly drew criticism from users who found the new interface confusing and cluttered, and OpenAI rolled back the change soon after , bringing the familiar ChatGPT interface back.

That wasn’t OpenAI’s only attempt to pull everything under one roof. The company has also shut down several stand-alone apps and folded their features directly into ChatGPT — a strategy that’s worked out better than the redesign did. ChatGPT Atlas, a stand-alone AI-powered web browser, lasted less than a year before being discontinued on August 9, with its most useful features absorbed into ChatGPT.

The company did the same thing with Operator , an AI agent that could browse the web and complete tasks on a user’s behalf, and OpenAI has increasingly built image generation directly into ChatGPT, shrinking the role of DALL-E as its own separate destination for creating images.
We also can’t forget its video-sharing platform, Sora , which struggled with high operating costs and user-retention challenges and shut down in March 2026.

When Apple unveiled Apple Intelligence in 2024, an improved Siri was one of the highlighted features. The pitch promised a Siri that could understand context, know what was happening across apps, and get tasks done effectively.

However, Apple repeatedly pushed back the release of the new Siri, citing various reasons like engineering issues and bugs . This delay eventually contributed to a $250 million settlement over claims regarding how Apple marketed the AI capabilities of the iPhone 16.
Siri AI finally appeared in the iOS 27 beta this past July, with the new AI-powered version rolling out to English-language users first this month; support for other languages is expected to follow.

Announced at its 2024 Build developer conference, Microsoft’s Recall feature was pitched as an AI-powered “photographic memory” for Windows PCs, periodically taking screenshots of what a user was doing so they could later search back through their own digital history.

Predictably, the announcement triggered an immediate backlash over privacy and security. Critics argued that Recall could create a searchable archive of highly sensitive information, including passwords, private messages, financial details, and other activity. Microsoft delayed the feature for nearly a year, giving the company time to rethink its security and privacy protections.

Even after a redesign, the controversy hasn’t gone away. A cybersecurity researcher recently built a tool that could extract and display data that Recall had captured, reviving questions about whether Microsoft has actually fixed the underlying problem.

Notion Mail launched in April 2025 as an AI-focused email product designed to help users organize and automate their inboxes. However, the company noticed its users were using separate AI agents to handle their email inboxes instead. As a result, Notion Mail is scheduled to shut down on September 22 .

The Humane AI Pin is probably one of the most well-known failures in AI hardware. Designed to provide AI features through a wearable device rather than a traditional smartphone, Humane raised $230 million from investors and garnered significant attention.

But the product struggled mightily with performance, and the situation worsened when Humane warned customers to stop using its charging case because of a potential battery fire risk. Humane then shut down its AI Pin business in February 2025, with most of the company’s assets acquired by HP for $116 million.

The Rabbit R1 was another heavily hyped AI device. Unveiled at CES in January 2024, the AI companion was designed to perform tasks on behalf of its owner. Rabbit said it had sold 100,000 units shortly after launch.
However, strong initial sales didn’t mean it was a strong product. Early reviews described the device as unfinished, with unreliable performance and a limited number of useful integrations.
body_zh: Relay 是一款人工智能驱动的工作流程自动化工具，作为 Zapier 的替代品，于 8 月份完全关闭。该产品允许用户使用 AI 代理自动化电子邮件和任务工作流程，但随着 OpenAI、Google 和其他更大的平台将类似的自动化直接构建到自己的工具中，已有五年历史的 Relay 很难坚持作为独立产品存在的理由。
最近，聊天机器人平台 Character.ai 在推出仅五年后就申请破产。
除了Character.ai 和Relay 之外，许多人工智能赌注甚至无法在构建它们的公司内部生存下来。根据标准普尔全球市场情报 (S&P Global Market Intelligence) 的数据，约 42% 的人工智能计划最终被其母公司放弃。原因各不相同：资金不足、技术挑战、竞争、扩展困难或用户需求疲软。
其结果是人工智能墓地不断扩大。以下是一些最著名的人工智能产品、初创公司、发布以及已经关闭、转向或严重低于预期的赌注。与其将其视为失败的记分卡，不如将其视为这些尝试可以（希望）教会其他行业的内容的记录。
即使是最大的参与者也不能幸免。 OpenAI 作为世界上最有价值的私营公司之一，也有过伤亡和失误。最近的例子之一是它试图将 ChatGPT 变成一个更广泛的“超级应用程序”。 7 月 9 日，OpenAI 更新了该应用程序，结合了多种体验，包括单独的“聊天”、“Codex”和“工作”模式，同时将传统的、熟悉的版本重命名为“ChatGPT Classic”。
重新设计很快引起了用户的批评，他们发现新界面令人困惑和混乱，OpenAI 很快就回滚了这一变化，恢复了熟悉的 ChatGPT 界面。
这并不是 OpenAI 唯一一次将一切都集中在一个屋檐下的尝试。该公司还关闭了多个独立应用程序，并将其功能直接合并到 ChatGPT 中——这一策略比重新设计的效果更好。 ChatGPT Atlas 是一款独立的人工智能网络浏览器，运行了不到一年就于 8 月 9 日停产，其最有用的功能被 ChatGPT 吸收。
该公司对 Operator 做了同样的事情，这是一个可以浏览网络并代表用户完成任务的人工智能代理，而 OpenAI 越来越多地将图像生成直接内置到 ChatGPT 中，从而缩小了 DALL-E 作为其自己的独立图像创建目的地的作用。
我们也不能忘记它的视频共享平台 Sora，该平台因高昂的运营成本和用户保留挑战而苦苦挣扎，并于 2026 年 3 月关闭。
当苹果在 2024 年推出 Apple Intelligence 时，改进的 Siri 是亮点功能之一。宣传中承诺 Siri 可以理解上下文，知道应用程序之间发生了什么，并有效地完成任务。
然而，苹果以工程问题和错误等各种原因一再推迟新版 Siri 的发布。这一延迟最终导致苹果就如何营销 iPhone 16 人工智能功能的索赔达成 2.5 亿美元的和解。
Siri AI 终于在今年 7 月出现在 iOS 27 测试版中，新的人工智能版本将于本月首先向英语用户推出；预计随后也会支持其他语言。
微软在 2024 年 Build 开发者大会上宣布，其 Recall 功能被定位为 Windows PC 的人工智能驱动的“照相记忆”，定期截取用户正在做的事情的屏幕截图，以便他们稍后可以通过自己的数字历史进行搜索。
不出所料，这一声明立即引发了人们对隐私和安全的强烈反对。批评者认为，Recall 可以创建高度敏感信息的可搜索档案，包括密码、私人消息、财务详细信息和其他活动。微软将该功能推迟了近一年，让该公司有时间重新考虑其安全和隐私保护。
即使在重新设计之后，争议也没有消失。一名网络安全研究人员最近开发了一种工具，可以提取并显示 Recall 捕获的数据，这再次引发了人们对微软是否真正解决了根本问题的疑问。
Notion Mail 于 2025 年 4 月推出，是一款专注于人工智能的电子邮件产品，旨在帮助用户组织和自动化收件箱。然而，该公司注意到其用户正在使用单独的人工智能代理来处理他们的电子邮件收件箱。因此，Notion Mail 定于 9 月 22 日关闭。
Humane AI Pin 可能是人工智能硬件中最著名的失败之一。 Humane 旨在通过可穿戴设备而不是传统智能手机提供人工智能功能，从投资者那里筹集了 2.3 亿美元，并引起了广泛关注。
但该产品的性能表现非常糟糕，当 Humane 警告客户因潜在的电池火灾风险而停止使用其充电盒时，情况变得更加糟糕。 Humane 随后于 2025 年 2 月关闭了其 AI Pin 业务，该公司的大部分资产被惠普以 1.16 亿美元收购。
Rabbit R1 是另一款被大肆宣传的人工智能设备。这款人工智能伴侣于 2024 年 1 月在 CES 上亮相，旨在代表其所有者执行任务。 Rabbit 表示，推出后不久就售出了 10 万份。
然而，强劲的初始销量并不意味着它是一款强大的产品。早期评论称该设备尚未完成，性能不可靠，有用的集成数量有限。
